findings.title: Improvements Should Be Made to Identify Students Eligible for Medicaid-Subsidized Services and to Recover Costs More Promptly
findings.description: TCPS has processes for identifying students eligible for Medicaid-subsidized services but needs enhancements to ensure all eligible children are identified and costs recovered timely. Fiscal year 2006 revenue for these services totaled $49,824 compared to $215,458 in fiscal year 2005.

dollar_amounts.context: Medicaid-subsidized services revenue fiscal year 2006
Medicaid-subsidized services revenue fiscal year 2005
Federal E-Rate funding approved for fiscal year 2006

findings.recommendation: TCPS should enhance its efforts to ensure that all students eligible for Medicaid-subsidized services are identified and that all eligible costs for Medicaid-subsidized services are fully recovered in a timely manner.

findings.title: TCPS Should Strengthen Internal Controls over Its Disbursements, Procurements, and Contract Monitoring
findings.description: Internal control deficiencies exist in the automated accounts payable and procurement system allowing unilateral processing by employees. Wire transfers were poorly controlled with $7.5 million processed without independent approvals. Competitive proposals were not obtained for architectural services ($840,000) and mentoring services ($71,000).

dollar_amounts.context: Accounts payable check disbursements fiscal year 2006
Wire payments processed by one individual July 2006 to March 2007
Architectural services not competitively procured
Mentoring services payments fiscal year 2006 without competitive proposals
Prepaid fuel contract amount fiscal year 2006
Credit card expenditures fiscal year 2006
Travel expenditures fiscal year 2006

findings.recommendation: TCPS should implement effective internal controls over its accounts payable and procurement system. TCPS should ensure that all contracts are procured in accordance with Board policies. TCPS should establish adequate procedures to ensure that fuel amounts invoiced are proper.

findings.title: Human Resource and Payroll Internal Controls Need to Be Strengthened
findings.description: Five employees had unlimited system access allowing them to add employees, change salaries, and process payroll checks without independent review. Workforce planning does not address non-instructional positions.

dollar_amounts.context: Direct salary and wage costs fiscal year 2006

findings.recommendation: TCPS should take the necessary corrective actions to ensure that adequate internal controls are in place over the human resource and payroll system. TCPS should expand its workforce planning to include non-instructional positions in critical operational units.

findings.title: Existing Controls Over Equipment Should Be Enhanced and Formal Policies Established
findings.description: TCPS did not have written policies for equipment tagging or physical inventories. Discrepancies were found between property records and assets on hand during testing of items costing $61,939.

dollar_amounts.context: Net book value of TCPS equipment June 30, 2006
Cost of equipment items tested for discrepancies
Computer equipment costing listed on records after disposal
Metal lathe recorded in records but could not be located

findings.recommendation: TCPS should develop and implement policies and procedures to ensure that accountability and effective control is maintained over all of its equipment.

findings.title: Steps Should Be Taken to Ensure Adequate Security Over IT Applications
findings.description: TCPS did not have a formal disaster recovery policy or comprehensive IT security policy. User access controls were insufficient and physical access to the computer room was not strictly controlled.
findings.recommendation: TCPS should implement appropriate security measures to safeguard its applications and data systems. TCPS should establish physical controls and safeguards over its computer operations.

findings.title: Certain Processes Should Be Implemented to Increase the Effectiveness and Efficiency of Maintenance and Custodial Operations
findings.description: TCPS had not established performance measures for maintenance operations. Preventive maintenance documentation was lacking. Energy management program cost-effectiveness needs verification.

dollar_amounts.context: Alternative funding obtained for St. Michael's Elementary School construction
Commitment toward Easton Elementary School renovation costs
Estimated construction costs for Easton Elementary School project
Energy cost avoidance November 2005 through January 2007
Total energy management program costs since July 2005

findings.recommendation: TCPS should enhance its maintenance and custodial operations by developing a performance measurement system. TCPS should periodically obtain and verify the contractor reports of cost savings of its energy management program.

findings.title: More Can Be Done to Ensure Cost Effective Operations
findings.description: TCPS has not conducted a cost-benefit analysis of operating transportation in-house. Smaller buses could be used on low ridership routes where current buses cost $20,000 more each.

dollar_amounts.context: Fiscal year 2006 student transportation costs
Additional cost per larger bus compared to conventional school buses
Average purchase price for smaller 66-passenger buses by other systems
Purchase price for 84-passenger buses purchased by TCPS in 2006

findings.recommendation: TCPS should take action to increase the cost-effectiveness of bus operations. TCPS should develop, track, and report to the Board appropriate and reliable performance measures.

findings.title: Internal Controls over Purchasing Could Be Improved
findings.description: Internal control weaknesses identified in food service purchasing procedures where independent verifications were not performed.

dollar_amounts.context: Excess of revenues over expenditures fiscal year 2006
USDA commodities received in fiscal year 2006

findings.recommendation: TCPS should ensure that each food supply invoice is verified as correct and supported by valid documentation establishing that goods were actually received.

findings.title: Additional Guidance or Policies Should Be Provided to TCPS Management
findings.description: The Board needs to develop, enhance, and adopt policies governing areas related to financial and support services including procurement, inventory, and transportation. School system management also needs to develop adequate administrative procedures in these areas.
findings.recommendation: The Board should provide increased financial and support service guidance to management by developing, enhancing, and adopting policies. In addition, the Board should ensure that related administrative procedures are developed by management as appropriate.

findings.title: The Board Should Consider Additional Steps to Assist It in Governing TCPS
findings.description: TCPS does not have an internal auditor reporting to the Board. The use of an internal auditor is a recommended best practice that can assist management in monitoring controls and conducting performance audits. A process such as a confidential hotline had also not been implemented for employees to report concerns.
findings.recommendation: TCPS should consider the feasibility of establishing an internal audit position and a hotline for the confidential reporting of operational issues and suspected fraud, waste, and mismanagement.

findings.title: TCPS Should Enhance and Enforce Its Code of Ethics Requirements for Filing Financial Disclosure Statements
findings.description: The Board's Ethics Policy does not require food service, transportation, and plant operations department managers to file disclosure statements despite their procurement responsibilities. In calendar year 2005, 4 of the 23 required personnel had not filed, and in 2006, 2 had not filed as of May 2007.
findings.recommendation: TCPS should expand its ethics requirements for filing disclosure statements to include all management employees responsible for procuring goods and services. TCPS should also actively monitor compliance with its Code of Ethics by verifying that all required financial disclosure requirements are met.

findings.title: Formal Investment and Debt Management Policies Have Not Been Established
findings.description: TCPS does not have a deposit policy to address custodial credit risk; $632,183 of the bank balance was exposed. TCPS has also not adopted formal policies governing management's use of long-term lease/purchase agreements or debt management as recommended by GFOA.

dollar_amounts.context: exposed to custodial credit risk
bank balance at June 30, 2006
long-term lease/purchase agreements totaled
outstanding debt to the State Retirement and Pension System of Maryland
total interest payments for all years

findings.recommendation: TCPS should adopt a formal policy governing cash investments and a formal policy governing long-term lease/purchase debt, in accordance with GFOA best practice recommendations.
